assessment.concept: Modern Italy in European and Mediterranean context
assessment.assessment: Renaissance Italy & Global Mediterranean studies Italian visual culture and cross-cultural exchange directly. European politics, modern history, social theory and research methods add relevant context, but do not sustain a sequence in modern Italian history, society, politics or national identity. Ancient Rome and Renaissance art do not supply modern Italian study.

assessment.concept: Italian literature, film and cultural interpretation
assessment.assessment: Comparative literary and film courses support close reading, genre, adaptation and visual analysis, and the Renaissance course gives real Italian cultural content. None of the selected evidence establishes an Italian literary corpus, a progression in Italian cinema or source work connecting these forms to modern Italy. The programme as a whole would study comparative culture more broadly.

Psycholinguistics examines comprehension, production, bilingualism and acquisition. Stylistics examines how grammatical choices shape meaning. Neither studies Italian grammar, language history or translation, and the current course reference supplies no Italian proficiency sequence or Italian-language research progression.

academicConstruction: The first trial replaces military history, US research and US media with closer Mediterranean and art-historical material, comparative policy and place in Europe. The second moves the Brain & Behavior prerequisite before Psycholinguistics in term two and Rhetoric in Action to term six, and uses visual and literary methods with the strongest available Italy-related course. Both pass 24-course, 180 EC, formal prerequisites and offering checks. They differ in course emphasis. Neither establishes recurring, documented inquiry into modern Italy. A language-methods direction also lacks Italian linguistic material after considering stylistics, psycholinguistics, comparative literature and the available foreign-language courses. The decision is academic and independent of the original offering conflicts.
distinctness: No UCR programme was selected, so the pairwise floor is not a gate. The separate trials isolate regional social inquiry and literary/media inquiry.
